STEAMBURGER STUDIOS

VoiceCleaner

User Manual

Clean, clear speech from noisy recordings: free, offline, for Windows and Mac. Start with the Quick Start.

VERSION 1.1.12 · NOVEMBER 2026

01Welcome

VoiceCleaner turns noisy, echoey or uneven speech recordings into clean, clear audio. It runs entirely on your own computer: no account, no subscription, no upload.

Open a recording (a phone memo, a Zoom call, a podcast take, the sound of a video) and VoiceCleaner removes background noise, room echo and hum, evens out the level and makes the voice clear. You compare before and after with an instant A/B switch, then export.

It is built for two jobs:

  • Cleaning recordings you already have, one at a time or a whole folder at once in the Batch tab.
  • Recording new material: single takes, whole sessions, or a script read from the built-in teleprompter, which you then join into one file in the Compile tab.
Your audio stays with you

Everything is processed on your computer. Nothing about you, your computer or your audio is sent anywhere. The only network requests VoiceCleaner makes are an optional update check and, if you ask for it, a one-time download of the voice re-synthesis model.

How to use this manual

If you just want a clean file, read the Quick Start: it takes about five minutes. The chapters after it explain each tab and setting in detail, and the last chapters are reference material: keyboard shortcuts, the command line, file locations and troubleshooting.

Names of buttons and menu items are written in this style, keys like Space, and file names like Episode 12 - Rec 001.wav. Where Windows and Mac differ, both are given; Ctrl is ⌘ Cmd on a Mac.

02Quick Start

From download to a clean, exported file in six steps.

1Install VoiceCleaner

Download the version for your computer from the latest release page on GitHub:

Your computerDownload
Windows 10 or 11, any PCVoiceCleaner-<version>-win64.msi
Windows with an NVIDIA graphics card (much faster)VoiceCleaner-GPU-<version>-web.exe1
Mac with Apple Silicon (M1 or newer), macOS 12+VoiceCleaner-<version>-macos-arm64.dmg

Run the installer (on a Mac, drag VoiceCleaner to Applications). Portable versions that need no installation are on the same page. VoiceCleaner needs 8 GB of memory.

“Windows protected your PC”

The downloads are not code-signed yet, so Windows may show this warning the first time.2 Choose More info → Run anyway. On a Mac, macOS may ask you to confirm opening it the first time.

2Start it and take the tour

A splash screen appears immediately and shows what is loading; the window opens once the AI engine is ready. The first time, a one-minute Getting Started tour points out the basics, one stop per tab. You can see it again any time from the ⋯ menu → Getting Started.

3Open a recording

Drop a file on the window, click Choose a Recording, or press Ctrl+O. WAV, MP3, M4A, FLAC, Opus, AIFF, WMA and the sound of video files (MP4, MOV, MKV, WebM) all work.3 The start screen also lists your RECENT files and the newest recordings of the current session for one-click access.

VoiceCleaner analyzes the recording as it opens: the noise, the room, hum, clipping and the level. If the recording starts with a moment of background noise before the first word, it learns that noise automatically.4

4Pick a preset

The settings sidebar on the right starts on the Clean Voice preset with Smart settings on. Smart settings uses the analysis to set Noise Reduction, Speech Enhancement and Room / Echo Reduction for this recording; those controls are marked AUTO. For most recordings you can go straight to Enhance.

If the recording is very noisy, choose Noisy Recording or Extreme Noise instead; for a podcast voice, Podcast. All presets are described in Presets.

5Enhance and listen

Click Enhance (or press Ctrl+Enter). Progress shows on the waveform and the sidebar shows the time left. When it is done, press Space to play, and A / B to switch between the original and the enhanced version at the same position.

Leave Equal-loudness comparison on: it plays the original at the enhanced loudness, so you judge the quality, not the volume.5 If you change a setting now, VoiceCleaner previews the change around the playhead; Enhance Again applies it to the whole recording.

6Export

Click Export Enhanced WAV… (or press Ctrl+E). The file is named after the original and saved to the session's Exports folder unless you choose another one. The original recording is never changed.

That is the whole workflow. To clean many files the same way, see the next page.

Bonus: clean a whole folder

  1. Open the BATCH tab and drop several files, or a whole folder, onto the window.
  2. Optional: turn on ◉ Preview (P) and click a file to hear a 10-second sample with the current settings. Adjust the sidebar until it sounds right.
  3. Choose where to save under Save to, then click Enhance All.
  4. When it finishes, Open Output Folder shows the results.
Quick-start keys
Ctrl+OOpen a recordingSpacePlay / pause
Ctrl+EnterEnhanceA / BOriginal / Enhanced
Ctrl+EExportRRecord / stop
Ctrl+TTeleprompterCtrl+/All shortcuts
Notes
  1. The GPU edition is a web installer: it downloads about 2 GB of NVIDIA CUDA libraries during installation, so it needs an internet connection the first time. ↩
  2. Code signing is a paid certificate that tells Windows SmartScreen who published a program. Without it, SmartScreen warns about any new download until it has seen enough installs. The installer is the same either way. ↩
  3. M4A, AAC, WMA, AMR and video files are decoded by the FFmpeg that ships with the Windows downloads. On a Mac they open once the Mac download includes FFmpeg as well; WAV, MP3, FLAC, Opus/OGG, AIFF and CAF open there already. See Supported input. ↩
  4. A third of a second of steady noise before the first word is enough. The learned profile is shown next to the button, under Noise Reduction; Clear Noise Profile undoes it. ↩
  5. Louder almost always sounds “better” to the ear. Matching loudness removes that bias from the comparison. ↩

03The Window at a Glance

One header, four tabs, and a settings sidebar shared by Enhance and Batch.

The header

  • Session: the current session (project). Click it for the session menu; see Sessions.
  • Teleprompter: opens the teleprompter. It shows when the teleprompter is open, and ● Recording while it records.
  • Activity chip: while something runs (enhancing, a batch, a preview), a chip shows it from any tab. Click it to go there.
  • Device and AI model: shown while the AI engine loads, and when something needs your attention: no AI model, the NVIDIA GPU chosen but not in use, or a faster edition available for this PC (for example CPU · RTX 5070 Ti found). Otherwise it is in Settings.
  • ⋯: the app menu.

The tabs

TabWhat it is for
ENHANCEOpen or record one recording, enhance it, compare A/B, export. Chapter 5.
PLAYBACKBrowse and play the session's recordings and exports, or any folder. Chapter 11.
COMPILEJoin enhanced takes into one file, with trimming and editing. Chapter 9.
BATCHEnhance many files with the same settings. Chapter 10.

A tab that is busy carries a badge (for example BATCH · 3/10). On Windows the taskbar button shows progress, and flashes when a long job finishes while VoiceCleaner is in the background. VoiceCleaner reopens on the tab you used last.

The ⋯ menu

  • Open Recording…, Open Recent (the last ten files), Export Enhanced Audio…
  • Audio Output: where all playback goes. See Settings.
  • Settings… (Ctrl+,): appearance, contrast, fonts, processing device and update checks.
  • Teleprompter…
  • Getting Started, What's New, Keyboard Shortcuts, Show Tips Again
  • Open Log Folder, Models and Licenses, Check for Updates…, About VoiceCleaner

On a Mac, every command is also in the menu bar (File, Edit, Playback, View, Window, Help), with its keys; About, Settings… and Check for Updates… are in the VoiceCleaner menu.

Quitting while VoiceCleaner is working (enhancing, exporting, running a batch or recording) asks first.

04Sessions

A session is a project folder: its recordings and exports stay together.

Start a new session for each episode, client or project. VoiceCleaner resumes the last session when it starts.

  • New Session… (Ctrl+Shift+N) creates Documents\VoiceCleaner Sessions\<name>\ with a Recordings and an Exports folder. A new session starts on the Enhance tab with nothing open; if the open recording was enhanced but not exported, VoiceCleaner offers to export it first.
  • Open Session… switches to another session.
  • Rename Session… renames the session and every file it created.
  • Open Session Folder and Open Default Recordings Folder show them in Explorer or Finder.

Every file a session creates carries its name, so files stay identifiable wherever they end up:

Episode 12 - Rec 003.wav           a recording
Episode 12 - Rec 003 enhanced.wav  its enhanced export
Episode 12 - Rec 004 append.wav    a take appended to it
Episode 12 - Compilation.wav       the Compile tab's result

Session names are limited to 32 characters and cleaned of characters Windows does not allow in file names.6

Notes
  1. Those are \ / : * ? " < > |. Keeping names short keeps full file paths well under the limits some older Windows tools still have. ↩

05The Enhance Tab

Two waveforms, one transport, measurements, and the settings sidebar.

Waveforms

The ORIGINAL track (purple) shows the recording as it is; the ENHANCED track (blue) shows the result. Each has its own Play button and volume. Click a waveform to move the playhead; Ctrl+mouse wheel zooms, and both tracks stay in step.

Selecting: drag across either waveform to select a passage. The playhead jumps to the start of the selection. A selection is used by Loop, by Learn Noise Profile, and by Live Preview.

Transport and A/B

  • Original / Enhanced (A / B): the switch is instant and click-free at the same position.
  • ▶ / ■ and Space play and stop; Home goes back to the start.
  • Loop (L) repeats the selection (or the whole recording) while you switch A/B or change settings.
  • Equal-loudness comparison plays the original at the enhanced loudness.
  • Learn Noise Profile, in the sidebar under Noise Reduction: select a part with only background noise (no speech) and click it. A learned profile is trusted, so that noise is removed more firmly. Clear Noise Profile undoes it.

Measurements

Under the transport, VoiceCleaner shows the original and enhanced values side by side:

MeasurementWhat it means
LoudnessIntegrated loudness in LUFS.7 VoiceCleaner targets −16 LUFS by default.
True peakThe highest peak, including peaks between samples, in dBTP.8
Noise floorHow loud the background is between words. Lower is quieter.
Speech-to-noiseHow far the voice stands above the background, in dB. Higher is cleaner.
Dynamic rangeHow much the level varies, in LU.
Speech ClarityAn estimated score from 0 to 100 and the improvement, with notes on what was detected. It is VoiceCleaner's own metric, not a standardized intelligibility score.

Live preview of changes

After the first Enhance, changing a setting re-processes about 10 seconds around the playhead (or your selection, up to 30 s) a moment after you stop adjusting. The previewed part is marked LIVE PREVIEW on the Enhanced track and plays at the level a full Enhance would give it. Enhance Again applies the settings to the whole recording; exporting first asks whether to do that.

Live preview is on by default with an NVIDIA GPU (about a second per preview) and on Apple Silicon Macs (under half a second, or about 5 s with Voice Re-synthesis). On other computers it can be turned on with the Live preview of changes checkbox, but it is slower.

Edit Take

Click ✂ Edit Take… above the Original track (or right-click a track, or press E) to cut out a pop, a click or a stumble. Select it, then Cut it (X or Delete, crossfaded) or Silence it (S, keeps the timing). Edits apply to both tracks, so A/B still compares the same audio, and they are used when you export. The original file is never changed; the edits are kept with the session and shared with the Compile tab. Clear Edits removes them.

Undo and redo

Settings changes can be undone with Ctrl+Z and redone with Ctrl+Y (or Ctrl+Shift+Z), or the ↶ ↷ buttons next to the preset. A slider drag is one step; the button's tooltip names the change.

Notes
  1. LUFS (Loudness Units relative to Full Scale) measures perceived loudness over the whole recording, per ITU-R BS.1770-4. −16 LUFS is the usual level for podcasts and online video; broadcast uses −23 (Europe) or −24 (US). ↩
  2. dBTP is decibels relative to full scale, measured as “true peak” (with oversampling), which catches peaks a plain sample meter misses. A ceiling of −1 dBTP leaves room for MP3 and streaming encoders. ↩

06Settings and Presets

A preset and three sliders cover most recordings. Everything else is there when you need it.

The sidebar is the same in the Enhance and Batch tabs. Every control is remembered between sessions. The mouse wheel scrolls the sidebar, even over a slider; click a control first to adjust it with the wheel. Double-click any slider to reset just that one.

Presets

A preset is a starting point. MODIFIED appears when you change a control; Reset goes back to the preset.

PresetUse it for
NaturalMinimal processing. Keeps the room and the voice as they are, just cleaner.
Clean Voice defaultBalanced cleanup for most recordings.
Noisy RecordingStrong noise reduction for fans, traffic and busy rooms.
InterviewModerate noise reduction, clearer speech, even levels between speakers.
PodcastBroadcast-style voice: enhanced, gently compressed, consistent.
Extreme NoiseMaximum AI enhancement and voice re-synthesis with artifact protection.

Your own presets: Save as… stores all current settings as a preset. The ⋯ next to it updates, renames or deletes it, or shows the presets folder. Presets are small JSON files, easy to back up or share.9

Smart settings

Smart settings: adapt to each recording is on by default. The analysis sets Noise, Speech and Room, and the controls tied to them, for each recording: clean recordings get light processing and noisy ones get more. While Smart is on, those controls are locked and marked AUTO, and a note explains why (the × hides the note; Show Tips Again brings it back). Turn Smart off to set them yourself; your values then stay as they are when you open another recording. Re-synthesis, leveling, EQ and the rest are always yours.

The three main sliders

Noise Reduction
Removes background noise such as fans, hiss, hum and room noise.
Speech Enhancement
Improves clarity: balances the tone of the voice and brings out presence.
Room / Echo Reduction
Reduces the sound of the room (reverb) and echoes.

Voice Re-synthesis

Re-generates the cleaned voice with a neural vocoder (NVIDIA BigVGAN). It smooths away leftover processing artifacts and restores natural harmonics. Off by default; 20–40% polishes the voice, while high amounts can change its character. The model (490 MB) is downloaded once from inside the app with Download voice model, then works offline.10

EQ & Tone

A live response curve, Tonal balancing (how much automatic correction toward a natural voice spectrum), Tilt (darker / brighter), and eight band sliders from 80 Hz to 10 kHz, ±12 dB. Double-click a band to reset it. If the EQ cuts the body of the voice (250 Hz–1 kHz) by 9 dB or more, a note warns that it can sound hollow or distant.

Dynamics

  • Leveling (amount, maximum correction, speed) evens out sentences and speakers over seconds, and holds still in pauses.
  • Compression (amount, threshold, ratio, attack, release) controls word-level peaks.
  • De-esser (50% by default) softens harsh “s”, “sh” and “t” sounds only at the moments they stick out.
  • Pauses: Shorten long pauses, off by default. See Shortening pauses.

Advanced

GroupControls
Noise reductionAI speech enhancement (on/off), Repair clipping, amount, noise floor estimate, spectral subtraction strength, noise gate threshold, residual noise floor, pause clean-up
Speech enhancementEnhancement strength, voice presence (around 3 kHz), high-frequency clarity (above 7 kHz), low-frequency cleanup
Room and echoReverb reduction, echo reduction
LoudnessNormalize loudness, target loudness (−30 to −10 LUFS, default −16), peak ceiling (default −1 dBTP)
Detected automaticallyWhat the analysis found: background noise and speech-to-noise, hum, room reverb, echo, voice pitch, high-pass filter and stereo layout; and Reset to preset
Tip: leave headroom for natural sound

Residual noise floor sets how far the background may be reduced. Keeping a little room tone sounds more natural than digital silence, which is why VoiceCleaner never removes all of it by default.

The quality check

Every result goes through a quality check that compares it with the original: lost syllables, a changed voice tone, high-frequency artifacts, over-compression, clipping, and pauses that came out louder than in the original. If it finds a problem, it reprocesses with gentler settings. The guiding rule is better speech, not obviously processed speech.

Notes
  1. Windows: %APPDATA%\VoiceCleaner\presets. Mac: ~/Library/Application Support/VoiceCleaner/presets. ↩
  2. Speed: about real time on a CPU (a 10-minute recording takes about 10 minutes more), about 3× real time on an Apple Silicon GPU, and much faster on an NVIDIA GPU. ↩

07Recording

Record a microphone, the computer's own sound, or both at once.

Click ● Record Audio on the start screen, ● Record on the Original track, or press R. The record panel opens above the Original waveform.

Choosing what to record

  • Microphone: any USB microphone, headset or line-in.
  • Desktop audio: anything playing through a chosen speaker or headphone output, so no “Stereo Mix” is needed.11
  • Both at once captures both sides of a call. The two are aligned and corrected for clock drift.

Each source has a level meter and a trim. ↻ Refresh devices picks up a microphone you just plugged in.

Options

  • 3-second countdown before recording starts. Click Record again to cancel it.
  • Record 1 s of room tone first: recording starts with a quiet second (Stay quiet, then Speak now), and that second becomes the noise profile, so the background is measured exactly.

Both are remembered between sessions.

Recording with a file already open

ModeWhat happens
New recordingThe take replaces the Original.
AppendThe take is added to the end of the Original.
OverdubThe take is layered onto the Original from the playhead, optionally while the Original plays (use headphones). Latency is compensated.

Where takes go

Takes are saved to the session's Recordings folder as 48 kHz 24-bit WAV, and streamed to disk while recording, so an unplugged microphone or a crash keeps what was captured. Combined results (append, overdub) are written as new files; the original is never changed.

No sound from the microphone?

Check that the operating system allows apps to use it: Settings → Privacy → Microphone on Windows, System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone on a Mac.

Notes
  1. On Windows this uses WASAPI loopback, which captures what an output device is playing. On a Mac it uses System audio on macOS 14.2 or later, or a loopback driver such as BlackHole on older versions. ↩

08The Teleprompter

Read your script while VoiceCleaner records, one take per section.

Open it with Ctrl+T, the Teleprompter button in the header, or Teleprompter on the start screen. Every take is kept and enhanced in the background with the current settings, and the Compile tab joins them in script order.

Writing the script

Paste or edit the script in the prompter (Edit, E), or open a .txt or .md file.

## 1 · Cold Open | The Hook
[B-roll: A/B toggle, noisy waveform snapping clean]
Listen to this. Now listen to this. Same recording, one click.

## 2 · The Why | Why I Built It
I record a lot of voice work: narration, devlogs, character lines.
  • ## Heading | Clip name starts a section. The clip name names its takes.
  • [brackets] are stage directions; D shows or hides them.
  • A blank line starts a paragraph.

Recording

Start (Space) counts down 3-2-1 and records from the chosen microphone without a break. When the next section reaches the reading line (or you press → / Page Down), a new take starts by itself. The cut is placed in the pause between the sections, so a word that runs over is never cut or repeated.

  • Retake (Backspace or Page Up) goes back to the start of the section and records it again. Every take is kept; the newest is used unless you mark one with Keep (G).
  • Last take (P) plays back the most recent take.
  • Step mode holds each section (or line) until you move on. Lines records one take per paragraph instead of per section, for line-by-line voice work.
  • Presentation clickers and foot pedals that send Page Up / Page Down work hands-free.
  • If the microphone sends only silence, a NO SOUND warning names it.

Teleprompter keys

SpaceStart / pause (pausing pauses the take)↑ ↓Speed (words per minute)
→ PgDnNext section+ −Text size
←Previous sectionMMirror (for teleprompter glass)
⌫ PgUpRetakeDStage directions on/off
GKeep this takeFFullscreen
PPlay last takeEEdit the script
HomeBack to the topHShow the key help
EscStop recording / leave fullscreen

The prompter's colours follow the app's day/night setting; the ◐ button keeps it always Dark or Light instead.

Takes are saved in the session's Recordings folder, named after the section, for example Episode 12 - 03 What It Does - Take 2.wav, enhanced into Exports, and listed in Compile.

09The Compile Tab

Join enhanced takes into one finished WAV.

Building the list

  • The list starts with the session's enhanced exports (Session Exports). Add more with Add Files…, by dropping files on the window, or with Add to Compilation in the Playback tab.
  • Teleprompter Takes shows the script instead: one row per section, in order, with its selected take (enhanced when ready). Right-click a row to use another take; it then counts as that section's keeper.
  • Drag rows to reorder, or use ▲ / ▼ or Ctrl+↑ / Ctrl+↓. Double-click a row to hear that take alone.

Options

  • Keep silence at each end: leading and trailing silence of every take is trimmed, keeping up to 100 ms (adjustable) so breaths and soft onsets survive. Short fades prevent clicks.12
  • Gap between takes: optional silence between takes.
  • Even out loudness between takes: matches the takes' loudness. A true-peak limiter keeps the result from clipping.
  • Shorten long pauses: see below.

The preview updates itself a moment after each change, so ▶ starts at once. Reordering while it plays keeps playing at the same take.

Editing and re-enhancing takes

  • ✂ Edit Take… (E or right-click): select a pop, click or a pause the trimming missed and Cut it (X / Delete) or Silence it (S). Ctrl+wheel zooms down to a few milliseconds; Hear Result plays the take as it will sound. Edits are saved in the session (compile_edits.json); the file itself is never changed.
  • ↻ Re-enhance (select several rows to do them all) enhances takes again from their original recordings, with the current settings or a preset, in the background. The replaced version is kept in Exports\Previous Versions; Revert to Previous Version swaps it back. Take edits stay in place.
  • Open in Enhance Tab loads one take's recording for fine-tuning; Update Take in Compile puts the result back.

Exporting

Export Compilation… saves to the session's Exports folder as <Session> - Compilation.wav.

Shortening pauses

Optional and off by default. Pauses longer than a threshold (1.0 s by default, 0.3–5 s) are shortened to a natural pause (250 ms by default, up to 2 s). The kept pause is made of the start and end of the original silence, joined by a short crossfade, so breaths survive and the background continues without clicks. Setting the length to 0 (“Remove completely”) removes long pauses entirely. Silence before the first word and after the last is left to trimming. It works in two places:

  • Compile tab: applied to every take before joining; rows mark the shortened pauses and the preview includes them.
  • Enhance tab (Dynamics → Pauses): applied when exporting, including Batch. The preview keeps the original timing, so A/B stays aligned. A note says how many pauses will be shortened and the time saved. Presets never turn it on.
Notes
  1. 5 ms fades at each cut. Short enough to be inaudible, long enough to avoid the click a hard cut makes. ↩

10The Batch Tab

Enhance a whole folder of recordings with the same settings.

  1. Drop several files (or a folder) anywhere in the window, or click Add Files…. Recordings in any supported format and videos work. Remove and Clear tidy the list.
  2. Set up the sidebar on the right: it is the same as in the Enhance tab, and Smart settings still adapts to each file.
  3. Optional: turn on ◉ Preview (P) and click a file to hear a 10-second sample of it (the part with the most speech) with the current settings. Compare it A/B at equal loudness (Space, A, B). The sample follows setting changes, so you can tune before enhancing everything.
  4. Choose Save to: This session's Exports folder, Same folder as each original, or Choose folder…
  5. Click Enhance All.

Each file is analyzed and enhanced on its own. A damaged file is reported and the rest continue. When it is done, Open Output Folder shows the results, and double-clicking a finished file opens it in the Enhance tab to compare. Results never overwrite an original. The Saved As column names each result.

To run batches without the window, for example from a script, see the command line.

11The Playback Tab

Find, play and route your recordings.

  • This Session lists the current session's recordings and exports.
  • All Recordings lists every session in the default recordings folder.
  • Browse Folder… scans any folder, including subfolders. Recordings and videos that can actually be played are listed; damaged ones are counted and skipped.

Search, sort, and play with a waveform and seek. Then send the selection on with Open in Enhancer, Add to Batch, Add to Compilation or Show in Folder.

12Export Formats

WAV for editing and archiving, MP3 for sharing.

OptionChoices
FormatWAV (recommended) or MP3
Bit depth (WAV)16-bit (dithered13), 24-bit (default), or 32-bit float
MP3 qualityHigh (VBR ~190 kbps), Standard (~130 kbps), Small file (~100 kbps)
Sample rateSame as original, or 44.1, 48 or 96 kHz

Exports are named after the original (also for phone memos and videos), which is never overwritten. Tick Show the file in File Explorer when done (Finder on a Mac) to go straight to the file; the choice is remembered.

Notes
  1. Dither adds a tiny, inaudible noise when reducing to 16 bits, which avoids the gritty distortion of plain truncation on quiet passages and fades. ↩

13Settings

How VoiceCleaner looks and runs. Open it with ⋯ → Settings… or Ctrl+, (on a Mac, VoiceCleaner → Settings…, ⌘ Cmd+,). Changes apply at once.

Day and night

VoiceCleaner follows the system's light/dark setting (Automatic). Choose Day or Night to keep one. Colours follow the Steamburger Studios website.

Contrast

When the system asks for more contrast (a Windows contrast theme, or Increase Contrast on a Mac), secondary text, borders and slider tracks become stronger. Always increase contrast does the same whatever the system setting.

Fonts

System fonts are used by default for readability. Brand fonts switches to the Steamburger Studios type: Bebas Neue, Syne and DM Mono.

Processing device

Automatic uses an NVIDIA GPU when there is one (on a Mac, the Apple GPU for re-synthesis); CPU only forces the processor. In use shows what processes the audio now, and the AI model.

Updates

Check for updates when VoiceCleaner starts; see Updates.

Audio output

⋯ → Audio Output selects System default or a specific output for every playback in the app, including take previews. Active outputs are listed first; disconnected or disabled ones are under Inactive. The choice is remembered. If a selected device is disconnected, playback pauses and the selection is kept: reconnect it and press Play, or choose another output. Finish recording before changing outputs or refreshing devices.

14Command Line

The Batch tab's processing, without the window.

On Windows, VoiceCleanerCLI.exe is next to VoiceCleaner.exe (by default in C:\Program Files\Steamburger Studios\VoiceCleaner).

VoiceCleanerCLI --batch recordings out --preset Natural
VoiceCleanerCLI --batch "Voice Memo 14.m4a" zoom_0.mp4 out --format mp3
VoiceCleanerCLI --batch D:\Podcast --recursive D:\Podcast\clean --preset Podcast --no-smart
VoiceCleanerCLI --list-presets
OptionMeaning
--batch IN… OUTInputs are files and/or folders; the last path is the output folder. Results are named <name>_enhanced.wav and never overwrite anything.
--recursiveInclude subfolders.
--preset NAMEA built-in preset or one of your own.
--no-smartUse the preset as it is, without adapting it to each file.
--format wav|mp3Output format.
--bits 16|24|32WAV bit depth (32 = float).
--device auto|cpu|cudaProcessor to use.
--list-presetsList the available presets.
--helpList everything.

It prints one line per file with progress and a summary at the end. The exit status is 0 when all files were enhanced, 1 when some failed (the others are still done), and 2 when there was nothing to do or the command had a mistake.

16Updates

VoiceCleaner checks for new versions, and installs them for you on Windows.

⋯ → Check for Updates… asks GitHub for the latest release. If there is a newer version, the app shows what is new. Nothing is downloaded or installed until you choose to, and nothing about you, your computer or your audio is sent.

  • Installed on Windows: Install Update downloads the installer inside the app (an interrupted download continues where it stopped), checks it against the checksum GitHub publishes,14 then offers Install and Restart or Install When I Quit. Windows asks for permission, the installer runs, and VoiceCleaner reopens and confirms the update.
  • Portable copies: Download opens the release page.
  • Mac: Download fetches and checks the DMG, then shows it in Finder; drag the new VoiceCleaner to Applications.

By default the app also checks once each time it starts and only speaks up when there is something new. Later hides that version until the next day; Skip Version hides it for good. Turn automatic checks off with the checkbox in the update window.15 After an update, a short What's New tour shows only what changed.

Notes
  1. A SHA-256 checksum is a fingerprint of the file. If even one byte differed from the published release, the check would fail and the update would not be installed. ↩
  2. Administrators can disable automatic checks entirely by setting the environment variable VOICECLEANER_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1. To test the connection from a terminal: VoiceCleaner --check-updates. ↩

17Reference

Supported input

  • Opened directly: WAV (including WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE, RF64 and W64), MP3, FLAC, Opus and Vorbis (OGG), AIFF and CAF.
  • Through the included FFmpeg: M4A and AAC (phone voice memos), WMA, AMR, and the sound of video files (MP4, MOV, M4V, MKV, WebM, AVI, WMV, 3GP). The first audio track is used; surround is mixed down to stereo.
  • Mono or stereo, 8 kHz to 384 kHz, up to 6 hours per file. Recordings too large for memory are processed from disk automatically.
Stereo contentHow it is processed
Identical channelsProcessed once as mono, written back as stereo
Speech on one side onlyThat channel is processed, then centred on both
Genuine stereoEach channel processed, with linked dynamics

How VoiceCleaner cleans speech

ProblemHow it is handled
Steady noise (fans, HVAC, hiss)A noise profile learned from pauses (or your selection), a Wiener filter, then the AI model
Changing noise (traffic, rustle, babble)DeepFilterNet3 neural speech enhancement
Clipping (recorded too loud)The cut-off peaks are rebuilt; every unclipped sample is kept
Clicks, taps, keyboard in pausesA transient suppressor that never touches speech
Electrical humAutomatic 50/60 Hz and harmonic detection, narrow notches
RumbleAdaptive high-pass, always below the speaker's lowest pitch
Room reverb, mild echoLate-reverb suppression using the measured reverb time;16 echo detection
Dull, muddy or boomy voiceAdaptive EQ toward a natural long-term speech spectrum
Leftover artifacts, thin voiceOptional neural voice re-synthesis (NVIDIA BigVGAN-v2)
Uneven levelsSpeech-aware leveling, a gentle compressor and an optional soft expander
Loudness−16 LUFS by default, true-peak limiter at −1 dBTP

Notes
  1. The reverb time (RT60) is how long the room takes for a sound to die away by 60 dB. VoiceCleaner measures it from the recording after removing noise. ↩

18Troubleshooting

Windows says “Windows protected your PC”.
The installer is not code-signed yet. Choose More info → Run anyway.
macOS won't open VoiceCleaner the first time.
Confirm opening it when macOS asks. If it only offers to move it to the Bin, open System Settings → Privacy & Security and choose Open Anyway.
The recorder shows NO SOUND or flat meters.
Allow microphone access in the system privacy settings (see Recording), check the trim, and click ↻ Refresh devices after plugging in a microphone.
Playback stopped and an output is shown as unavailable.
The selected output was disconnected. Reconnect it and press Play, or pick another one in ⋯ → Audio Output.
An M4A or video file won't open on a Mac.
Those formats need FFmpeg, which the Mac download does not include yet. Convert the file to WAV first, or use the Windows version.
Enhancing is slow.
On a CPU, processing (and especially Voice Re-synthesis) takes longer. Use the GPU edition on a PC with an NVIDIA card, check ⋯ → Processing device, and keep Re-synthesis at 0% unless you need it.
The header says the AI model is not installed.
VoiceCleaner still works with its own spectral noise reduction. Reinstalling restores the model; ⋯ → Models and Licenses shows what is installed.
Export asks “Your settings changed since the last Enhance”.
You changed a setting after enhancing. Choose to enhance again so the export matches what you hear in the preview.
The voice sounds thin, hollow or “underwater”.
Lower Noise Reduction or try the Natural preset, raise Residual noise floor's room tone, and check the EQ warning for cuts to the 250 Hz–1 kHz range.
Something else went wrong.
Open ⋯ → Open Log Folder and attach voicecleaner.log to an issue on GitHub. The log contains no audio.

Known limitations

  • De-reverberation is statistical: it clearly reduces room tails but cannot make a very reverberant room sound fully dry.
  • Clipping repair rebuilds peaks clipped by a few dB; very hard clipping comes out much better but not like an undistorted recording.
  • Speech buried under very loud noise cannot be fully recovered. The quality check favours keeping speech over removing the last bit of noise.
